title: Laser assisted cold spray of AISI 4340 steel

preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: sanded with a P-80 grit sandpaper, then washed with soapy water and rinsed with isopropyl alcohol

experimentalProperties.Raster_Pattern: After a raster was completed, the nozzle would turn around and repeat the same raster in reverse laying down an additional layer on top of the cold-spray deposit. Six layers were deposited in this way. The nozzle moved up in the z direction by 0.1 mm between each layer

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: highly deformed, flattened particles commonly found in other micrographs of CS deposits

experimentalProperties.Laser_System: LDM-4000-100 variable power (maximum 4 kW) diode laser

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: little noticeable change from CS deposit

Experiments.Notes: CS sample laser heating to 500 C

preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: sanded with a P-80 grit sandpaper, then washed with soapy water and rinsed with isopropyl alcohol

experimentalProperties.Raster_Pattern: After a raster was completed, the nozzle would turn around and repeat the same raster in reverse laying down an additional layer on top of the cold-spray deposit. Six layers were deposited in this way. The nozzle moved up in the z direction by 0.1 mm between each layer
experimentalProperties.Laser_System: LDM-4000-100 variable power (maximum 4 kW) diode laser

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: powder particles deformed, but the substrate deformed as well, so that the bottoms of the impacted particles maintained some of their roundness. As the surface temperature increased further, the powder particles implanted themselves deeper into the substrate.
